<!-- Reminder: No private information on this page! -->'''TL;DR:''' Within a span of two days, we observed high latency and database errors on '''<code>mw-{api-int,parsoid, jobrunner}</code>''', all of which are deployments supporting MediaWiki <u>for non-user-facing purposes</u>. Our '''External Storage''' cluster experienced a significant load increase and a high number of connections. '''Notably, user-facing traffic was little impacted by this incident'''  

During the scheduled PHP 8.1 '''Scap rollout''' for <code>mw-{api-int,parsoid,jobrunner}</code>, on March 12th & 13th 2025, we found ourselves having said deployments running '''without access to the Memcached cluster''' and '''without a valid prometheus StatsD address'''. 

Without '''Memcached access''', MediaWiki had to query the databases for objects that would typically be cached, leading to '''increased database load'''. At the time, MediaWiki was pushing stats to both Graphite and <code>prometheus-statsd-exporter</code>, thus the lack of a valid prometheus statsd address had no impact.  

During the incidents, we observed '''high load and a sharp increase in connections''' to the '''External Storage''' cluster, while the majority of MediaWiki errors (<code>channel: error</code>) visible at the time, were database related. The '''External Storage''' hosts are used to store the compressed text content of wiki page revisions 

However, there was an '''overwhelming volume of memcached errors''' events (<code>channel: memcached</code>, ~2mil/min) which logstash was unable to process quickly enough, <u>resulting in an observability gap where</u><u>:</u>

* Logstash itself probably was not able to render the <code>channel:memcached</code> logstash dashboard, until after the incident, allowing it to consume all its backlog
* Delays in the <math>\texttt{mw} \rightarrow \texttt{logstash} \rightarrow \texttt{prometheus-es-exporter}\rightarrow  \texttt{prometheus}</math> pipeline pipeline caused the  '''[[gerrit:plugins/gitiles/operations/alerts/+/refs/heads/master/team-sre/mediawiki.yaml#48|MediaWikiMemcachedHighErrorRate]]'''  alert to be missing, while the corresponding Grafana graph displayed no data during the incidents.

==Detection==
Our working theories were:

* High traffic from specific network/client
* Scheduled jobs that went awry
* Greedy changeprop-jobqueue jobs 

All the above are the usual suspects when we experience MediaWiki latency and/or Database load. Detection was not easy here, for reasons explained in “what went wrong”. However, we were able to thoroughly sort out what went on after the fact.

== Contributing Factors ==
Key factors that contributed in causing this incident, as well as delaying its root cause, were: scap, php-fpm envvars.inc include file, and the logstash-prometheus pipeline.

=== What does Scap do? ===
[[Scap]] is our deployment tool for MediaWiki. Scap takes care of 3 very important steps:

* build and push MediaWiki images
* Update <code>helmfile-defaults</code> with the latest image version tag '''per deployment, and per release'''.
** The image flavour (if it is a 7.4 or a 8.1 image) of each deployment-release combination is defined in puppet in [[gerrit:plugins/gitiles/operations/puppet/+/refs/heads/production/hieradata/role/common/deployment_server/kubernetes.yaml#261|<code>kubernetes.yaml</code>]]
* Runs <code>helmfile</code> on all deployments running MediaWiki

To provide a visual example, the latest scap run updated the  helmfile-defaults for the main release of mw-parsoid (aka mw-parsoid-main) as follows: <syntaxhighlight lang="yaml">
docker:
  registry: docker-registry.discovery.wmnet
main_app:
  image: restricted/mediawiki-multiversion:2025-03-18-101751-publish-81
mw:
  httpd:
    image_tag: restricted/mediawiki-webserver:2025-03-18-101751-webserver
</syntaxhighlight>

=== What is this <code>envvars.inc</code> include file in php-fpm? ===
We are exporting two very important environmental variables to php-fpm

* <code>MCROUTER_SERVER:</code> static IP address defined in deployment-charts, essentially the memcached/mcrouter address, defaults to <code>127.0.0.1:11213</code>
* <code>STATSD_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_SERVICE_HOST</code>: populated and injected into pods by the k8s api, unset by default


In kubernetes, we put both variables in a <code>ConfigMap</code> called <code>mediawiki-main-php-envvars</code>, which in turn mount in the container as  <code>/etc/php/</code><code><X.Y>/fpm/env/envvars.inc</code>

PHP-FPM reads the environmental variables from a hardcoded include directory, whose exact location depends on the PHP version. 

In the <code>'''publish-74'''</code> container image, that would be:<syntaxhighlight lang="bash">
[www]
listen = ${FCGI_URL}
<snip>
; MediaWiki helm chart via the php.envvars value.
include = /etc/php/7.4/fpm/env/*.inc
</syntaxhighlight>In the <code>'''publish-81'''</code> container  image, that would be:<syntaxhighlight lang="bash">
[www]
listen = ${FCGI_URL}
<snip>
; MediaWiki helm chart via the php.envvars value.
include = /etc/php/8.1/fpm/env/*.inc
</syntaxhighlight>

=== So, what was broken then? ===
Our PHP 8.1 <code>mw-{api-int,parsoid,jobrunner}</code> rollout consisted of two sister patches: 

* [[gerrit:1126607|1126607]]<sup>[puppet]</sup> '''switching'''  <code>mw-{api-int,parsoid, jobrunner}</code> the MediaWiki image flavour '''from <code>publish-74</code> to  <code>publish-81</code>'''
* [[gerrit:1126650|1126650]] <sup>[deployment-charts]</sup> which in practice would change the '''mount location of <code>envvars.inc</code> from <code>/etc/php/7.4/fpm/env/envvars.inc</code> to <code>/etc/php/8.1/fpm/env/envvars.inc</code>'''

We performed a scap deployment to deploy the above. Our expectation was that <u>after the deployment, was that we would have:</u>

* <code>mw-{api-int, parsoid, jobrunner}</code> running the <code>mediawiki-multiversion publish-81</code> image and 
* The <code>mediawiki-main-php-envvars</code> <code>configMap</code> mounted as  <code>/etc/php/8.1/fpm/env/envvars.inc</code>

Due to an unexpected Scap behavior, explained below, '''what was actually rolled out in production was''' :

* '''<code>mw-{api-int,parsoid,jobrunner}</code> running the <code>mediawiki-multiversion publish-74</code>'''
* '''The <code>mediawiki-main-php-envvars</code> <code>configMap</code> , mounted at <code>/etc/php/8.1/fpm/env/envvars.inc</code>'''

As the PHP 7.4  image (publish-74) was in use, the includes under /etc/php/7.4/fpm/env/*.inc, <u>contained default values,</u> so they were not useful.

=== How did we break this? ===
During the scheduled deployment, the Scap command was executed with the flag <code>-Dbuild_mw_container_image:False</code>. This flag is commonly utilised by Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) as, '''in most cases, our changes do not necessitate rebuilding container images'''. Specifically, transitioning the main release of <code>mw-{api-int, parsoid, jobrunner}</code> to the <code>publish-81</code> image would not require an image rebuild as we have already <code>publish-81</code> built and cached. 

However, this '''transition would necessitate updates to the <code>helmfile-defaults</code> of the main releases for <code>mw-{api-int,parsoid,jobrunner}</code>''' so to replace  the latest -<code>publish-74</code> image tag with the latest -<code>publish-81</code> . Unfortunately, it was  not immediately apparent that using the flag <code>-Dbuild_mw_container_image:False</code> '''would additionally cause scap to skip the <code>helmfile-defaults</code> update.'''

==Conclusions ==
Never run deploy to production while listening to [[:en:Bonnie_Tyler|Bonnie Tyler]]. Especially [[:en:Holding_Out_for_a_Hero|Holding Out for a Hero]]

====== "What" dashboards vs "Why" dashboards ======
Many of the dashboards we have assigned to alerts, point to a dashboard exhibiting the "What". For instance, our "[https://grafana.wikimedia.org/d/U7JT--knk/mediawiki-on-k8s Not enough idle PHP-FPM workers for Mediawikii]" alert, points to a dashboard where we can see there many busy PHP workers, and potentially that we are serving some errors. Those alone give very little information as to *what* may have caused this. 

It would have made a difference if we had alerts linked to dashboards showing graphs of components that depend or impact each other. For example, high mediawiki latency may be related to high external traffic, or increased edge cache misses. In a similar manner SQLBlobStore keys are directly related to External Storage.  

While we have Runbooks attached to several alerts, we could consider working on "Why" dashboards which would not only provide a more holistic overview of a group of components, but have the relevant links that could work as breadcrumbs.  

====== We must learn to coordinate incidents better ======
During the incident, we had some of our '''best engineers''' '''available'''. However, ensuring effective coordination among all responders proved to be tricky.

* The Incident Coordinator found it difficult to coordinate responders effectively during the incident as it '''wasn’t clear who was working on what''' and whether multiple people were independently following the same venues of debugging. 

* Furthermore, there was some '''ambiguity as to when people were joining the Incident Response and when there were parting''', making it difficult for the Incident Coordinator to track active participants and areas of focus.

* The '''channels were somewhat noisy''' with input being shared, at times, without context, while also interspersed with discussions not directly related to the IR process. This puts extra burden on the IC to effectively consolidate and interpret key information.

* Our '''assessment of the external user impact''' was not comprehensive. While there was a perception that the situation was critical, external services were minimally affected. A better estimation of the impact would help align our response appropriately.

* We need to be able to '''interface with MediaWiki developers''' during incidents and have their perspective at hand.


====== Are all of our Alerts serving us well? ======
Our Alerts were not as useful we would like. First and foremost, the alert that would point us to the right direction -<code>MediaWikiMemcachedHighErrorRate</code>- either resolved immediately. '''On May 12th, during the incident, we had 78 alerts firing, albeit not for 78 different things. There is a high chance that even if the <code>MediaWikiMemcachedHighErrorRate</code> had fired, we might have see it as a side effect, and thus, not acted on it.'''

====== We are not using trace.wikimedia.org during incidents ======
Good work has been put to https://trace.wikimedia.org/, however, we didn't utilise it during this incident, though it may have been useful 

===What went well===
We had a lot of people available to help, each on specialising in different areas.

===What went poorly?===
The technical root cause of this incident is not the primary concern. What is more relevant are the reasons that prevented us to detect, even from the March 12th incident, that 3 of our MediaWiki deployments were operating without access to the Memcached cluster. On March 12th, we assumed that the scap rollout was not the problem. By March 13th, we were certain that it was the scap rollout after all, but it was challenging to understand how it contributed to the incident.  

===Where did we get lucky?===

* There was little impact to external users
